blocks.title: Risk Identification, Assessment, and Analysis comparison
Risk Identification, Assessment, and Analysis exam shortcuts
items: Risk described as Low / Medium / High → QUALITATIVE
Qualitative analysis uses categories and rankings.
Example: Phishing risk is rated High.
Use numerical analysis when costs and frequencies are provided.
Example: Once every four years = 0.25 ARO.
Question asks chance vs consequence → LIKELIHOOD vs IMPACT
Likelihood is probability; impact is severity.
Example: Rare but catastrophic = low likelihood, high impact.
blocks.example: Watch for formula clues, recovery-time wording, and the difference between broad risk appetite and specific risk tolerance.

questions.q: A risk is rated Low, Medium, or High using a risk matrix. Which type of analysis is this?
questions.explanation: Qualitative analysis uses descriptive categories or rankings.

questions.q: A risk assessment calculates expected annual losses in dollars. Which type of analysis is this?
questions.explanation: Quantitative analysis uses numerical or monetary values.

questions.q: An asset is worth $200,000 and the exposure factor is 25%. What is the SLE?
A loss event is expected once every four years. What is the ARO?
questions.explanation: ARO expresses annual frequency. Once every four years equals 0.25 per year.

questions.q: A risk has an SLE of $40,000 and an ARO of 0.5. What is the ALE?
A security team performs a risk assessment after a newly disclosed critical vulnerability affects its environment. Which assessment type is this?
questions.explanation: Ad hoc assessments are performed as needed in response to a specific event or concern.

questions.q: A company performs the same formal risk review every quarter. Which assessment type is this?
questions.explanation: Recurring assessments happen on a regular schedule.

questions.q: A cloud security platform continuously reevaluates risk as configurations change. Which assessment type is this?
questions.explanation: Continuous assessment reevaluates risk on an ongoing basis.
